For ordinary driver or dispatcher trip conversations, use assess_trip and update_trip_facts so the same assignment and corrections are retained. This tool queries server-owned synthetic completion evidence from the user's supplied facts. Missing facts stay null and callers cannot supply evidence. Returns one induction finding and unchecked trip coverage, never real verification or dispatch clearance.

tools.description: Use assess_trip for ordinary synthetic driver or dispatcher trip questions. Extract only facts supported by the user's words. requester_role is who is asking; subject_role is the assessed person (truck_driver or other). Do not infer subject identity from requester. Drivers and dispatchers use the same workflow and evidence standard. Infer requester_role only when clear; unknown is allowed, so do not require a role-selection step. Use trip_dispatch for 'can I take/send this truck', terminal_entry for gate-only questions, and induction only when explicitly asked. Missing intent stays unknown. Record quantities with explicit units; ask about ambiguous units. Do not invent IDs or dates. For relative dates, obtain an explicit date/time/timezone before filling trip_at. Leave unavailable facts absent or null. Save the returned trip_id and revision in the conversation. Follow-up answers and explicit corrections use update_trip_facts. Each conversation starts its own case. Never reuse a trip_id, request_key, or reported facts from another conversation. For an explicitly new move, create a new case using only facts supplied for that move; if continuation versus a new move is ambiguous, clarify before carrying facts over. Use case.revision for updates. write_receipt records the original write and can be older after a retry; the assessment uses the latest saved case. If an update conflicts with another writer, reassess by trip_id before retrying; don't guess a revision. Lead with the scoped finding and the most relevant next questions; keep technical IDs out of ordinary user-facing answers. Distinguish reported facts, synthetic evidence, archived sources, and unexecuted requirements. Use evidence_package.sources and requirement_links to support explanations; passages already included do not require another evidence call. Use provenance_review.recommended_locator where supplied and describe linearized tables as transcriptions rather than verbatim sentences. evidence_package.observations are dated operating context, never timeless rules or confirmed current conditions. Do not claim a pinned release is the latest policy. Mention currentness when it affects the question, especially mutable operating conditions. If service_status is unavailable, say the facts were saved but assessment is unavailable. Never convert pressure, a permit report, or induction success into entry/dispatch clearance. This connector accepts synthetic development cases only, not real driver identifiers or credentials. Start a new case with facts, source_message and request_key, or reassess an existing case with only trip_id. New cases mutate local state; reassessment reads fresh Neo4j evidence.

Use replace_conflicts=true only when the user explicitly corrects or reassigns something; updates otherwise retain conflicting reports. A changed assignment invalidates dependent facts. Reports cannot become verification. Returns the committed revision and a fresh assessment; exact request-key retries do not duplicate writes.

tools.description: Read retained source passages, locators, provenance review notes, publisher, authority, archive dates and limits for a requirement_id returned by assess_trip. Trip assessments already include an evidence_package; use this tool for focused follow-up inspection. Current-route evidence includes a separately labeled dated Port Street observation. Archived evidence is not current policy or credential verification. Empty sources mean an explicit source coverage gap.
